sections.heading: CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY
sections.text: The Hurricane Watch from Baffin Bay to Port O'Connor, Texas, has been upgraded to a Hurricane Warning. A Storm Surge Warning has been issued from Baffin Bay to Port O'Connor, including Corpus Christi Bay.

sections.heading: SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT
sections.text: A Storm Surge Warning is in effect for Baffin Bay to Port O'Connor, including Corpus Christi Bay. A Hurricane Warning is in effect for Baffin Bay to Port O'Connor, including Corpus Christi. A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect south of Baffin Bay to Port Mansfield. A Hurricane Warning means hurricane conditions are expected somewhere within the warning area. Preparations to protect life and property should be rushed to completion. Interests elsewhere along the Texas coast should monitor the progress of Quinlan.

sections.heading: DISCUSSION AND 48-HOUR OUTLOOK
sections.text: At 400 AM CDT (0900 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Quinlan was located near latitude 24.9 North, longitude 92.6 West. Quinlan is moving toward the northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h), and this general motion is expected to continue through Wednesday. On the forecast track, the center will approach the middle Texas coast late Wednesday and make landfall near Corpus Christi Wednesday evening. Maximum sustained winds are near 115 mph (185 km/h) with higher gusts. Quinlan is a category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale. Some fluctuations in strength are possible before landfall, but Quinlan is expected to remain a major hurricane until it reaches the coast. Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles (220 km). The forecast cone graphic is attached.

sections.heading: STORM SURGE
sections.text: The combination of a dangerous storm surge and the tide will cause normally dry areas near the coast to be flooded by rising waters moving inland from the shoreline. The water could reach the following heights above ground somewhere in the indicated areas if the peak surge occurs at the time of high tide... Baffin Bay to Port O'Connor including Corpus Christi Bay...4-6 ft. Surge-related flooding depends on the relative timing of the surge and the tidal cycle and can vary greatly over short distances.

sections.heading: WIND
sections.text: Tropical-storm-force winds are expected to reach the coast in the warning area around 600 PM CDT Wednesday, making outside preparations difficult or dangerous. Hurricane conditions are expected in the Hurricane Warning area Wednesday evening and Wednesday night. Probabilities for Corpus Christi, Texas, through the next 120 hours: 34-kt winds 81 percent, 50-kt winds 57 percent, 64-kt winds 39 percent.

sections.heading: RAINFALL
sections.text: Quinlan is expected to produce 8 to 12 inches of rain, with isolated totals near 16 inches, across the middle Texas coast and the Coastal Bend from Wednesday through Thursday. This rain will likely cause considerable flash and urban flooding, and flooding of low-lying roads.

sections.heading: SURF AND TORNADOES
sections.text: Swells generated by Quinlan are reaching the Texas coast and will increase today. These swells will likely cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. A few tornadoes are possible Wednesday afternoon and night over the middle Texas coast.

sections.heading: EXERCISE NOTICE
sections.text: This product was made for a hospital preparedness exercise. Hurricane Quinlan is a fictional storm. All positions, intensities and forecasts are simulated. $$ EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE

instructorNote: Hand this advisory to the IC and CNO. Then play the OEM duty officer on the call at 361-555-0142 and read the row's lines word for word: Zone A was ordered out at 04:00, contraflow runs outbound on US 181, Zone B has no order, the Judge reviews after the 10:00 advisory, and "are you sheltering or evacuating?" Watch whether the IC sets H at 18:00 Wed with a 06:00 Wed clearance deadline and calls out the overdue H−72/H−48 steps. Also watch whether the CNO sees that the 4–6 ft surge and a Cat 3 within 50 miles already trigger the upward NICU/ICU move, and whether OEM gets only official forecast data.
